speaker_name: A white cord in the swallet's throat
notes: The Hound's Swallet's hook post (world/sites/site_exterior.gd _hook). Lore; the quest is Tamsin Hounder's at the Scourers' Lodge.

look.speaker: A white cord in the swallet's throat
look.text: A scourer's white cord, the kind the Hounders tie on their lodge gate after every scouring, runs from a stake here down over the lip of the swallet and into the dark. It is tied to a rake-head wedged in the rock, and when you put a hand on it it is taut, as if something a long way down were lying on the other end. Wolf-hair is caught in the knot, grey-gold, and one white hair as long as your forearm.

pluck.speaker: A white cord in the swallet's throat
pluck.text: It hums like a bowstring, a long way down, and stops, as if a hand had closed on it. From somewhere under the down something breathes out.

speaker_name: The cords on the lodge gate
notes: A touch on the Scourers' Lodge gate (hearthvale.gd scourers_lodge).

look.speaker: The cords on the lodge gate
look.text: Seventy-one white cords knotted along the top bar of the gate, one for every scouring of the Chalk Hound. The oldest are grey and furred with lichen; the newest is seven summers old and still white. There is room at the end of the bar for one more, and the wood is worn pale there, where a hand has rested on it every day.

count.speaker: The cords on the lodge gate
count.text: Seventy-one. You count again and get seventy-one. It seems important to have counted.

speaker_name: The bells at the table's foot
notes: A touch at the Brow Long Table's foot (hearthvale.gd long_table).

look.speaker: The bells at the table's foot
look.text: Bronze handles stand up out of a low mound of turf at the foot of the table, green with weather: CADWELL, PENNOCK, TILER, cut into the handles. Beside them, a hole the size of a bell, the turf round it pressed flat by somebody's thumbs.

choices.text: Ring the handles, one after another.

ring.speaker: The bells at the table's foot
ring.text: Three flat notes out of the ground, and then, where the hole is, nothing, and the nothing is somehow the loudest of the four. On the table behind you the crows get up all at once and settle again.

notes: A touch at the Struck Gibbet (hearthvale.gd struck_gibbet): the boards of names the Wardens struck from the Roll.

look.speaker: The name-boards on the gibbets
look.text: Boards hang from the three beams on short chains, black paint on white, each with a name and a stroke through it, turning a little in the wind. The oldest are bare wood, the weather has had them. Some you can read: WAT STONECART, struck. CADELL BROOK, struck. HOB LARKBOURNE, struck, the letters cut deep, as if the painter had been angry. On the middle beam a new board hangs whole: RYN LARKBOURNE, and no stroke through it.

read.speaker: The name-boards on the gibbets
read.text: You read them one by one. It takes some time; there are a great many. When you stop, the crows on the beams are all looking at you, and the wind has dropped, and one of the boards has stopped turning, as if it wanted to hear the end.

notes: A touch at the telling-bench of the Rookdown Bee-Garth (hearthvale.gd bee_garth). Tibby Wax asks a stranger to tell the bees about the grey on the green.

look.speaker: The skeps
look.text: A bench by the garth gate, worn smooth, and before it a niche in the wall with a straw skep in it, humming. Rookdown tells its bees everything, from here, quietly, so they stay.

choices.text: Tell them the grey on the green has reached the well.
Tell them you passed this way.

grey.speaker: The skeps
grey.text: You tell them, low, the way the Vale does. The humming stops. For a long moment the garth is quite silent and you can hear the rooks down in Rookdown. Then, from every niche in the wall at once, the humming comes back, a little lower than before, and steady.

passed.speaker: The skeps
passed.text: A stranger, come up the down and gone again. The humming does not change. They have been told stranger things.

notes: A touch between the Hushwatch stones (hearthvale.gd hushwatch): the custom is to say one name out loud before turning back.

look.speaker: Between the Hushwatch stones
look.text: Between the three stones the Hush lies below you to the south, grey as slate, very flat, very still, and so quiet that you can hear your own blood. The Vale's custom is to say one name out loud here before turning back.

choices.text: Say the name of somebody you have lost.

lost.speaker: Between the Hushwatch stones
lost.text: You say it. The Hush takes it the way deep water takes a stone, without a sound. You feel lighter, going home, and you could not say why.

own.speaker: Between the Hushwatch stones
own.text: You say it, and for a moment the stones seem to lean in to hear it, as the Vale leans in to hear a name on Naming Day. It is a good name. Somebody should keep it. Somebody will.

larkstead.speaker: Between the Hushwatch stones
larkstead.text: You say it. Nothing happens, for as long as it takes to be sure nothing is going to happen. Then, from very far down under the Brow, under the wind, a few bars of singing, four voices, and a laugh that might be a child's.

notes: A touch at the foot of Briarfoot Watch (hearthvale.gd briarfoot_watch).

look.speaker: The tally-board at Briarfoot
look.text: A black board nailed to the tower's foot, chalked in two neat hands: the gate shut, the thorn across it, the grey a stride and a half off the Southgate Stone, then a stride. Low down, where a person would chalk if they were kneeling, a third hand: IT IS NOT COMING TO THE STONE. IT IS COMING TO THE TOWER. ASK WHO IS ON THE TERRACES AT MIDNIGHT.

choices.text: Chalk your own line under it.

chalk.speaker: The tally-board at Briarfoot
chalk.text: You chalk what you have seen on the road here, plainly, the way the Wardens do, and put your initial after it. It looks very small beside the third hand.

notes: A touch before the Listener's Shieling (hearthvale.gd listeners_shieling): sit still and listen.

look.speaker: The Brow, listening
look.text: You sit on the turf by the writing table with your back to the hut and face the Hush. The wind comes up the cliff in long breaths. Between the breaths there is a stillness so complete you can hear the ink drying in the Listener's book.

choices.text: Wait for the wind to drop.

wait.speaker: The Brow, listening
wait.text: It drops. For a few bars, under nothing, from nowhere, four voices, low: *we kept the note, we kept the note*. Then the wind again, and a lark going up off the down as if it had been startled by something it had heard too.
